| [CLAIM-113](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-113.md) | Transformations and invariants define one another: translation preserves some structures exactly, carries some equivariantly, preserves some approximately and reorganizes others, and identity is studied through what a class of transformations leaves invariant | A105's reframing after U37, and the manuscript §4 and §11: "Structural transformations help identify structure through what they preserve", with a four-way split of exact, equivariant, approximate and reorganizing transformations. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-114](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-114.md) | Drift along a reconstruction chain can be marked by a pragmatic phase change, the first generation at which a different communicative configuration dominates, which per-step error does not show | A73, recovered: track local reconstruction error D_local(i) = W(q_(i-1), q_i) apart from cumulative departure D_global(i) = W(q_0, q_i), and look for the generation at which the configuration flips. Dropped when the latents were demoted at U28, without critique. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) | What survives translation is the set of communicative distinctions and relations a receiving system can still reconstruct and act upon, not the wording or the proposition | The manuscript's central thesis (Abstract, §1, §12). | [CLAIM-117](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-117.md) | Pragmatic fidelity requires preserving the dynamics of interpretation, not only final judgements: a good transport approximately intertwines source and target framing operations | A30's commuting diagram for pragmatic fidelity, developed in the manuscript §9 as intertwining defects and the commutator-distortion identity. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-118](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-118.md) | Context and interpreter are separate sources of interpretive change: in-context conditioning changes the effective decoding context, adaptation changes the decoder, and improving the signal differs from improving the interpreter | A43's first point about the U17 proposal, developed at A44–A45 into three sources of change (evidence, transient computation, parameters). | [CLAIM-119](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-119.md) | Communicative categories form a concept lattice rather than a hierarchy: categories such as affectionate teasing and sarcastic condemnation share attributes and differ in a few social-relational constraints | A75 §7, recovered: formal concept analysis as the direct formalization of the owner's "objects are intersections of regions". Absent from A81, C6 and the manuscript without critique. The record holds Ganter and Wille unread. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-124](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-124.md) | Communicative objects are characterized through overlapping constraints on observables at partially ordered levels; translation transports these locally constrained structures, and repeated reconstruction changes both local interpretations and their global compatibility | The thesis of proposal v5 (A81–A83, under U30), which put observational structure first: "a global communicative object is no longer stipulated in advance."
